content: Health indicators in Uganda, as a developing country, are significantly behind global averages. Recent data indicates that the life expectancy at birth in Uganda is approximately 49 years. The child mortality rate, defined as the number of deaths before the age of five, is alarmingly high, with 140 deaths per 1,000 live births as of 2002. Uganda was severely impacted by the HIV/AIDS epidemic that swept through East Africa. However, by the end of 2003, Uganda had implemented the most effective national response to AIDS among African nations, achieving a notable reduction in prevalence rates (see AIDS in Africa for further context). In 2003, the Ugandan Ministry of Public Health reported a cholera outbreak in the Bundibugyo district. The majority of cases were concentrated along the Semliki and Lamia rivers, highlighting the geographical spread of the disease in this region. Uganda is also home to the Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI), which is recognized as one of the most advanced viral research facilities in East Africa. This institute plays a critical role in the study and management of viral diseases in the region.
